newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to delay issuing sterling Eurobond-paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to delay issuing sterling Eurobond-paper.

text.p: Brazil has decided to delay the launch of a 10-year 200 million sterling Eurobond expected for this week because of fears the proceeds may be confiscated by the courts, a newspaper said.

The legal fears arose following news of a Milan court of appeals ruling that ordered the seizure of Brazilian government assets, including the proceeds of a 500 billion lira June 2 bond issue, Gazeta Mercantil said.

Gazeta said the proceeds of the lira bond were not confiscated because the court order was issued too late, but the Brazilian government preferred to wait in the case of the sterling bond issue until the legal situation was resolved.

Brazilian central bank officials said the second reason for delaying the Eurobond issue was an expected rise in British interest rates this week, which would increase the costs of the bond issue, Gazeta said.

The Milan court ruling springs from a British high court order in 1990 which judged in favour of four coffee trading companies suing the Brazilian government over outstanding debts of the now-extinct Brazilian Coffee Institute (IBC).
The IBC only partly repaid debts before ceasing to exist in 1990 when the Brazilian government assumed all outstanding obligations.
--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
